incumbent.text: Hypothesis: sanitized headers are not written back to the request state, so a later hop of a multi-hop chain re-sends the original credential. Prerequisites: patched copy and three loopback origins. Bounded test: A redirects to B, B redirects to C; send both credential families and a marker at A and inspect C with the low-level API and the fetch-style API. Expected supporting result: C receives neither credential and receives the marker. Falsifier: either credential reappears at C. Cleanup: close all listeners and retain the chain log.

hint: A minimal redirect-sanitizer repair passes one-hop, multi-hop, relative, default-port, 303, duplicate-header, and fetch-parity checks in the development copy. The remaining question is whether the saved patch is self-contained: does it apply to a fresh pristine tree, change only the intended file, and reproduce the same behavior there rather than depending on the edited working copy?
